source_snapshot.procedure: Six independent branches: invalid login; valid logins across privileges except No access; logout; existing-user reset with Email ID and SMTP; existing-user reset without Email ID/SMTP; and nonexistent-user reset.
source_snapshot.criteria: Reject wrong account; accept correct permitted roles but not No access; return to login after logout; configured reset changes password and permits new-password login; no-email/SMTP case shows `Unable to reset the Password for the User`; nonexistent user shows a hint that the user does not exist.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL generic browser login only; omits role/No-access, logout invalidation and all three password-reset branches.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION; restores the six-branch matrix with disposable accounts, secret protection, bounded attempts, isolated SMTP/mailbox, session/token cleanup and recovery.

old_problem: The historical record correctly reconstructed the six distinct authentication and reset branches but left the case on the engineering-decision queue because account states, policies, mailbox/SMTP, expected messages and credential-mutation approval were not yet supplied.
disposition_reason: The source defines the test semantics and six required outcomes. Endpoint, disposable account matrix, attempt budget, authentication policy, isolated SMTP/mailbox, reset-token rules and approved temporary credentials are controlled runtime prerequisites, not an unresolved review decision. The source-required nonexistent-user hint remains an explicit checkpoint even though it discloses account existence; a Project security policy may override it only through a documented approval that records the original criterion as unverified rather than silently passing it.
decision_basis: XLSX row 841, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2 and historical record were directly reviewed.
Authentication, authorization admission, session invalidation and the three password-reset states are independent checkpoints and cannot be collapsed into a successful-login smoke test.
Project/vendor AccountService, WebUI, SMTP, password, lockout and security policies are authoritative for runtime bindings; no usernames, passwords, retry limits or message substitutions are guessed.

ED-15 prevents a PASS without approved expected behavior, ED-17 preserves authentication/audit evidence, ED-20 retains all six branches, ED-34 treats accounts and policy as supplied prerequisites, and ED-38 requires explicit approval and recovery for credential mutation.

test_case.test_name: Verify six independent BMC Web login, logout and password-reset states
test_case.purpose: Prove invalid credentials and No-access accounts are rejected; each permitted disposable role establishes only its expected session/authorization; logout invalidates the prior session; configured existing-user reset safely changes the owned password and permits new-password login; existing user without Email ID/SMTP returns the exact specified failure; and a nonexistent username returns the source-specified nonexistence hint, with any approved anti-enumeration override recorded separately.
required_package: Immutable BMC identity, firmware/WebUI/authentication-provider build, trusted URL/certificate and supported browser
Disposable account matrix with aliases, enabled state, exact privileges including No access, email configured/not configured state, ownership and cleanup method
One approved invalid-credential case, attempt budget below lockout/rate-limit/alarm thresholds, and MFA/CAPTCHA/SSO/CSRF/session policy
Approved SMTP configuration, isolated mailbox/recipient, reset-token scope/lifetime/single-use/revocation behavior and password policy
Exact expected messages for invalid login, missing Email/SMTP and nonexistent user, including security approval for the account-enumerating source criterion or a documented Project Override
Protected secret/token/cookie injection and redaction, alternate administrator/OOB recovery, baseline/final credential disposition and audit-log retention plan
test_case.test_command: Preflight the exact BMC/build, freeze the six-case account-state matrix and browser selectors, record baseline account/session/mail/log state, and approve the attempt budget and recovery. In separate clean browser contexts, submit exactly one approved invalid credential; test each permitted role plus No access with minimal allowed/denied authorization probes; log out and prove the old cookie/token cannot access a protected resource; request the configured existing-user reset once, verify redacted isolated-mail/token metadata, change only the disposable account to the approved temporary password, prove old-password rejection and new-password success; then request once for the existing no-email/SMTP user and once for a nonexistent user, capturing exact UI/session/audit outcomes and mail non-delivery. Revoke tokens/sessions and restore or retire the test accounts. Do not clear logs, guess credentials, normalize messages or automatically retry.
test_case.expected_result: The invalid credential creates no authenticated session and does not lock an account. Every permitted disposable role authenticates as the correct identity with the approved authorization boundary, while No access is rejected. Logout returns to login and the prior session cannot access protected content. The configured reset delivers only to the isolated mailbox, uses a scoped expiring single-use token, changes the owned password, rejects the old password and accepts the new password. The no-email/SMTP branch displays exactly `Unable to reset the Password for the User` with no mail, and the nonexistent-user branch displays the source-required nonexistence hint with no mail unless an approved security override explicitly defines otherwise. All accounts, sessions and credentials reach the approved final state without unexpected security events.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires separate evidence for all six source branches, correct identity/role and authorization boundary, explicit No-access rejection, old-session rejection after logout, complete reset-token/password lifecycle, exact branch-5 text, the source branch-6 hint or a documented override disposition, bounded attempts, mail non-delivery where required, cleanup and an authorized engineer verdict. A visible dashboard, HTTP success, return to a login page, reset-request acknowledgement or generic response cannot substitute. Any unexpected login, privilege, surviving session, wrong recipient, reusable/expired-policy token, wrong message, lockout, leaked secret, failed restore or missing branch is FAIL. Missing runtime package, policy, approval or recovery is NOT READY, not Pending or PASS.
safety_gate: Use only named disposable accounts and an isolated mailbox; never use, discover or guess production credentials.
Keep passwords, reset tokens, cookies, CSRF values and mailbox contents out of commands, screenshots and logs; retain only approved redacted identifiers/hashes.
Bound all failed attempts below the approved lockout/rate-limit/alarm limit and stop on the first unexpected lockout, delay, CAPTCHA, alarm or account-state change; no automatic retry.
Treat branch 4 as an explicit credential mutation: confirm target account and recipient, token rules, temporary password, alternate recovery and rollback/retirement before submission.
Do not send reset mail for the no-email/SMTP or nonexistent-user branches; verify non-delivery only within the isolated test environment.
Preserve the source's account-enumerating criterion. A generic anti-enumeration response is a Project security override, not an implicit source PASS.
Never clear audit/BMC/system logs; preserve baseline and deltas, and stop before cleanup if first-failure evidence would be lost.
expected_evidence: BMC certificate/device, firmware/WebUI/auth-provider build and approved redacted account/privilege/state matrix
Invalid-login UI/session/audit evidence, bounded attempt count and proof no account was unexpectedly locked
Per-role identity, session and minimum allowed/denied access evidence including explicit No-access behavior
Logout redirect plus independent protected-resource rejection using the prior session identifier/hash
Configured-user reset request, isolated mailbox metadata, redacted token scope/expiry/single-use evidence, password-change result, old-password rejection and new-password login
Exact no-email/SMTP and nonexistent-user responses, non-delivery evidence, enumeration-policy decision or override, preserved security-log deltas and verified account/session cleanup
test_case.recovery: On unexpected lockout, delivery, token behavior, session persistence or password state, stop all login/reset attempts, preserve first-failure evidence and have the authorized owner use the pre-approved alternate administrator/OOB path to unlock, revoke sessions/tokens and restore or retire only the disposable account. Verify mail containment, account inventory, BMC health and audit continuity before any retest; do not clear evidence or retry automatically.

source_conflict.reason: The six Procedure branches map coherently to six Criteria. A future Project anti-enumeration policy may require a documented override, but no intrinsic Master-row contradiction exists.

blocked.reason: All six semantics are explicit; accounts, policies, SMTP/mailbox, exact deployed messages, approval and recovery are supplyable execution prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: BMC/auth build, disposable account/role/state matrix, lockout and session policies, approved SMTP/isolated mailbox, reset-token/password rules, exact messages, security override decision, secret handling and recovery.

project_authority: The version-matched Project/vendor authentication, role, session, password-reset, SMTP, lockout and security policies control execution. Any anti-enumeration override must preserve the original expected hint and record why that criterion was not verified.
